_comment: Clip-worthiness questions for the `rate` command. Same instructions-file format clefcut-cloudflare-remotion-video uses: questions (CLEF question objects), pass (defect threshold per question id), escalate_margin, severity, escalate_only. Every question is worded so a HIGH value means a problem is present; visual_energy's score levels run from most energetic (0) to most static (4) for the same reason.

opens_on_action.instructions: The image is a contact sheet of one candidate segment; cells run in time order and span the whole segment. Does the segment open on throat-clearing, greetings, filler words such as 'so' or 'and', or dead air, so that no real content appears within roughly the first second?

complete_thought.instructions: Does the segment fail to read as one complete, self-contained idea from start to finish, for example by covering only half of an idea or by drifting between two separate topics?

ends_clean.instructions: Does the segment end mid-sentence, mid-word, or in the middle of a visual action, so that the ending feels chopped off rather than finished?

needs_context.instructions: Would a viewer who sees only this segment be confused because it refers to people, events, numbers, or earlier statements that are never shown or explained inside the segment itself?

visual_energy.instructions: Rate the visual energy of the segment for a sound-off, scroll-fast feed. Level 0 is the most energetic; level 4 is a frozen screen.
criteria: Strong visual energy: frequent motion, action, expressive faces, or on-screen text that keeps changing
Moderate visual energy: regular cuts, gestures, or text changes
Mild visual energy: one mostly static shot with occasional movement
Minimal visual energy: a nearly frozen screen
No visual energy: a single static screen, like a still image
